approvalTitle: Agent activity diagram: requirements (7 open questions, 10 readings, 7 language gaps)
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, 2026-10-09, verbatim. Its sixth bullet under *The sequence* stops in the middle of a sentence; Q5 asks how it ends.

> Create a new spec workflow specification called an "Agent Activity Diagram" (.aad). It is a tool that is intended to provide developers a unified overview of where what work is happening.
>
> For this it shows a diagram with the following elements:
>
> * Projects.
> * Agents / Threads
> * Specifications
> * Tasks
> * Environments
> * Locations (Branch + Worktree)
>
> The sequence is always as follows.
>
> * A project can have one or more active specifications. A toggle option allows the user to also show archived specifications.
> * A specification can have a status: Pending, Progressing, Input Required, Finished, Archived.
> * A specification has a set of tasks, these are not dedicated elements but rather listed items inside the specification element. They are grouped in: "Progressing" , "Pending", "Input Required", "Finished", and provide collapsing and expanding capability. By default the progressing and "input required" groups are expanded, and the other other ones are collapsed. The state of each element group is also persisted.
> * A specification element can have relations to one or more agents. but each agent can at any given time only have one relation to a specification.
> * Each agent then can (or rather should) be connected (i.e. have a relation) to one or more elements that depict a Folder "Worktree" and "Branch" combination. i.e. the work is always done on a branch, and can be done on a worktree. If no worktree is used then the folder is "Default". This element should be called a 'location' and visualized as one element with a horizontal line that splits the two fields. i.e. the top one is the branch. and the bottom one is the folder. each of these locations also can have a set of Pull requests added. Similar like the tasks in the specification these are not standalone elements, but rather listed items available in a collapsible/expandible form inside the 'location' element.
> * This 'Location' element can always have only two relations. one towards an agent/thread, and one towards an environment. No other relations are possible.
> * A 'Environment' element depicts a system on which the work will happen. For example a local machine (ours is often Fractal). Or it could be a cloud environment, for example the Claude Code cloud environment. Or it could be a container or WSL system. Important is that the
>
> Layouting:
>
> * The user has the option to position elements, of which then their position gets persisted. However he can also right click and unlock the position after which the layouting will be done automatically. The idea is that a gravity based, outwards radiating layout is used, through which the projects start in the middle, the specifications surround them, and then the Branch+worktree connect a specification to one or more environments (where the work is done at).
>
> Also:
>
> * Each of the elements and list items should also have an optional 'link' symbol that uses hyperlinks for quick navigation to the designated web page, file location.
> * The user can add/change/remove elements and relations using toolbox entries. But the intent is that the agents will update the view as a sort of central view of what work is going on where.
> * Write this down in a notion definition, so that future other implementations can interpret it. Use the same patterns as for the other [tools], so also think about examples etc.

The last bullet's final sentence is changed in one place, marked with square brackets: the request's word there names one kind of tool, and this repository's terminology check reads it as all of them.

**It is a diagram.** Its elements are connected, so by ADP terminology its kind is Diagram, it is specified in DISL, and its definition belongs beside the other diagram types. Its display name is **Agent activity diagram** and its origin `etalii/agent-activity-diagram`, ADP's own notation as the functional decomposition graph and Agent Behavior Modelling are. It is not in the catalogue yet (`docs/tools.md`); Requirement 10.8 adds it.

**Two repositories, and the definition comes first.** The diagram type is defined in [etalii.adp](https://github.com/etalii-adp/etalii.adp), where the languages and the tool definitions live and where the other hosts read them; this host implements that definition. Requirement 1 is delivered there as pull requests, before the work here that depends on it.

**Two writers.** Every other diagram in this host is drawn by a person. This one is mostly written by agents and read by a person, and the person's own contribution is where things are placed and what is folded away. Requirements 6 and 8 follow from that.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Activity file** | The `.aad` file: one file holding one agent activity diagram. |
| **Registration** | The `.adp` file beside an activity file, which identifies it to this host. |
| **Project** | An element: one body of work, such as a repository or a product. |
| **Specification** | An element: one piece of specified work in a project, with a status and a list of tasks. |
| **Task** | A list item inside a specification, with a title and a status. Not an element: it has no position and no relations. |
| **Agent** | An element: one worker on a specification. The request calls it "Agent / Thread"; a thread is the same thing seen from a project chat, and this document says agent for both. |
| **Location** | An element: where an agent's work is, as a branch and a folder. The folder is the worktree's, or `Default` when the work is in the repository's main checkout. |
| **Pull request** | A list item inside a location. Not an element. |
| **Environment** | An element: a system the work happens on, such as a local machine, a cloud environment, a container or a WSL system. |
| **Group** | A collapsible heading inside an element with the list items under it: one per task status in a specification, and one for the pull requests of a location. |
| **Link** | An optional address on an element or a list item: a web page or a file location. |
| **Locked** | Said of an element whose position the user set. An element that is not locked is placed by the automatic layout. |
| **View state** | What the user sets about how the diagram is shown and that is kept: locked positions, which groups are collapsed, and whether archived specifications are shown. |
| **Finding** | As in ADP terminology: something a reading reports about a file, with a severity and a place. |

## What the request leaves open, and how this document reads it

Each is a reading, not a ruling. Striking one changes only the criteria named with it.

| # | Reading | Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | A specification belongs to exactly one project. | 3.1 |
| R2 | An agent with no specification is allowed (an idle agent), and so is a location with no environment yet. Both are reported at severity info, since the request says an agent "should" be connected. | 3.3, 3.7 |
| R3 | A specification's status is stored as written. It is not computed from its tasks. | 2.2 |
| R4 | A pull request has a title and a link and no status of its own, and a location's pull requests are one collapsible group, collapsed by default. | 2.5, 4.5 |
| R5 | A location has one link for its branch (a web page) and one for its folder (a file location), since it shows two fields. Every other element and every list item has one. | 5.1 |
| R6 | A task and a pull request each have an id, so that an agent can change one item without rewriting the list. | 2.6 |
| R7 | An environment has a kind: local machine, cloud, container, WSL or other. | 2.5 |
| R8 | Dragging an element locks it. A locked element shows a small lock symbol, so the user can tell which ones the layout will not move. | 6.2, 6.3 |
| R9 | Hiding archived specifications hides those elements and their relations and nothing else. | 4.7 |
| R10 | Positions the automatic layout computes are never written to the file. Only locked positions are. | 6.6 |

## Which languages apply

- **DISL** specifies the diagram type: `agent-activity-diagram.dis`, with `agent-activity-diagram.md` beside it for what DISL cannot say. DISL is at version 0.3 (draft, 2026-10-06).
- **FBL** declares how the activity file is read and written, if Q2 is ruled as this document assumes. FBL is at version 0.2.
- **DID** is the stored form of a diagram built on DISL when the specification declares no other. Q2 offers it as the alternative.

## Whether the languages suffice

The coordinator's brief asks for every shortfall to be reported as a language-extension finding. DISL 0.3, DID 0.2 and FBL 0.2 were read on etalii.adp's `origin/develop` at `da64ff0` against what Requirements 2 to 6 need. **This is a reading of the specifications' text, not a trial with a definition**; the design repeats it against a draft `.dis` before any extension is proposed. Where a row says *searched*, the words searched for are in the design's notes and the absence is a search result, not a proof.

**What DISL already covers.** The five element types and their fields, with defaults and required fields (sections 4.3, 4.6); tasks and pull requests as list values of a structured type (4.3, 4.4); lists inside an element with a title, a collapsible heading, an icon per item and add, remove and reorder (6.9); an element drawn as two fields with a separating line (6.9); a status that changes an element's look (4.5, 6.6); which element type may connect to which, with every other pair refused (4.9, 8.7); at most one relation at an end, refused in a gesture (4.9, `std.multiplicity`); toolbox entries and context menus (7.1 to 7.3); the file extension `.aad` (3.2); and ids an agent may write by hand (11.5.1).

**What it does not.**

| # | What the diagram needs | What the languages have | Blocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | **A list grouped by a field's value**, under one collapsible heading per value, with items still editable. | No group-by (searched). Four separate lists, each a filter over the tasks, can imitate it; whether items can be edited through a filtered list is not stated (6.9). | 4.2, 4.3 |
| D2 | **Collapse state kept per element and per group, with a default per group.** | DID keeps `collapsed` per element and per list (DID section 3). How a declared default and a stored value interact is not stated. Under FBL the registration keeps positions only (FBL 8.3), so nothing is kept. | 4.4, 4.5 |
| D3 | **A switch on the canvas whose value is kept** (show archived). | A switch exists (`canvas.filters`, 6.13.1), but "its value is viewer state" and viewer state must not be written (11.6). A stored diagram attribute can drive visibility, but no canvas control binds to one. | 4.6, 4.8 |
| D4 | **Lock and unlock as gestures.** | The flag exists and is stored (`pinned`, 11.6, DID section 3) and a layout can respect it (section 10). No declared way to set or clear it (searched): the `view` action takes only `collapsed`, `filters` and `viewpoint`. | 6.2, 6.4 |
| D5 | **A layout that radiates outwards with one ring per element type.** | `force` and `radial` are names passed to an engine, "and its result is the engine's" (section 10, B.10). Nothing assigns a type to a ring (searched). Declaring layouts is listed as open (D.2, item 9). | 6.5, 6.7 |
| D6 | **A link that opens**, on an element and on a list item, to a web page or a file location. | A `uri` type, a clickable label and a conditional badge with a click exist (4.2, 6.9, 6.12). No open action in the closed action set (9.4, searched); no click or link on a list item; file paths as against URIs are not addressed. | 5.2 to 5.6 |
| D7 | **One storage that keeps view state and also says what happens when another program changes the file.** | DID keeps `pinned` and `collapsed` and says nothing about outside changes (searched). FBL specifies the reload (7.3) and keeps only positions. | Q2, Q3, 8.1 |
| D8 | **A finding when a file written outside ADP breaks "at most one".** | Findings for a stored breach are stated for endpoints only (8.7); for multiplicity it is an inference. A declared invariant (8.3) makes it certain without a language change. | 3.8 |

Requirement 1.4 turns each of D1 to D7 into a decision for the user before anything is added to a language. D8 needs none.

## What was measured

Read on 2026-10-09: this repository on `develop` at `fae8ab1e`, and etalii.adp on `origin/develop` at `da64ff0`.

| Subject | State | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A diagram module's shape | **Exists**: `api`, `backend`, `client`, `examples`, and `definition` for one that derives from DISL | `src/diagrams/readme.md` |
| Deriving a diagram from a bundled `.dis` | **Exists**: toolbox, menus, property rows and findings, for Agent Behavior Modelling | `src/diagrams/agent-behavior-modelling/definition`, `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` |
| Reading and writing a YAML body through FBL | **Exists** | `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` |
| Showing a change made outside ADP in an open diagram | **Exists** for the diagram family | `DiagramDocumentChangeHandler`, `DiagramDocumentReloadBridge` in `EtAlii.Adp.Diagram` |
| Layouts the canvas library has | **Manual, tree and row-packed.** No force-directed or radial one. | `src/client/src/canvas/library/layout/layoutAlgorithm.ts` |
| A layout dependency in the client | **None found** under the names d3, elk, dagre or force | `src/client/package.json` |
| List items or collapsible groups inside an element | **None found** in the canvas library's definition types. A search, not a proof; the design establishes it. | `src/client/src/canvas/library/definition` |
| Locking an element's position | **None found** under the names pinned, pin, locked or unlock in the canvas library and `EtAlii.Adp.Diagram` | same |
| A link on an element | **None found** | same |
| Revealing a workspace path from the canvas | **Exists** | `revealPath` in `ContextConnectionProvider.tsx` |
| Where a definition's examples live | In this host's module, not in etalii.adp; the definition's `.md` describes them | `definitions/diagrams/functional-decomposition-graph.md` in etalii.adp |
| A published corpus of agent activity | **None known.** The notation is new, so the examples are written for ADP. | Requirement 9 |

## Open questions

Each is a selection. The option marked **(default)** is what this document is written against until the user rules otherwise.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | "Write this down in a notion definition": what is written, and where? | **The tool's page in the Notion "Tools" database, and the tool definition in etalii.adp (default):** the page says what the diagram is for and how it functions, in prose, as the user asked for the Knowledge designer on the same day ("write the idea and how it should function in the notion tools page so that other implementations can benefit from it"); `agent-activity-diagram.dis` and `.md` under `definitions/diagrams` follow from this specification's design, as every other diagram type has them. · **The Notion page only:** no definition files until a second host asks for them. · **A definition for the Notion host:** how the diagram is kept as a Notion database, one row per element. That is a further specification, for etalii.adp.ide.notion. · Other. | 1.1, 1.8, 10.8 |
| Q2 | Write the activity file as what? | **YAML of ADP's own schema, through an FBL binding (default):** short, line-based and easy for an agent to edit one entry of; an edit is a splice; FBL already says what happens when another program changes the file. View state then has to be ordinary content of the file (Q3). · **A DID definition in JSON, with the extension `.aad`:** needs no binding and already keeps lock and collapse state; more verbose for an agent to write, and DID says nothing about outside changes. · Other. | 2.1, 2.7, 8.1 |
| Q3 | Keep view state (locked positions, collapsed groups, show archived) where? | **In the activity file, in a part of its own (default):** one file tells everything, as the user ruled for the Knowledge designer; agents leave that part alone. A click that folds a group is then a change to a file agents also write. · **In the registration:** the activity file holds only what agents report, and a user's view never collides with an agent's edit; view state is then per registration and does not travel with the file alone. · Other. | 4.4, 4.8, 6.1, 8.6 |
| Q4 | Have agents update the diagram how? | **By editing the activity file, from a published description (default):** `agent-activity-diagram.md` describes the file completely enough to write by hand, a JSON Schema is published, and an instruction text an agent can be given is shipped with the examples. Nothing to install. · **Through a command ADP provides** (a command-line tool or an MCP tool) that makes each change: safer against malformed files, and a second thing to build and keep in step in every host. · Other. | 8.2, 8.3 |
| Q5 | The request's sentence on environments ends at "Important is that the". Finish it how? | **Nothing further is required (default):** an environment has a name, a kind and an optional link. · **An environment is one element however many locations use it:** already so in this document (Requirement 3.5). · **An environment is told apart from a location on sight** by its shape and colour: already so (Requirement 7.2). · Other: the user completes the sentence. | 2.5, 3.5 |
| Q6 | Connect an agent to a second specification: do what? | **Refuse, with the reason (default):** as this host does for the functional decomposition graph; the user removes the first relation themselves. · **Move the agent:** the new relation replaces the old in one undoable step, which is what happens when an agent changes work. · Other. | 3.2 |
| Q7 | Where the languages fall short (D1 to D7): do what, as a rule? | **Extend the language, each construct named for what it does (default):** decided gap by gap under Requirement 1.4, so the other hosts read a definition and not prose. · **State it in the `.md` and in `x-` keys or a plugin for now**, and propose extensions later: faster, and the other hosts get a description instead of a definition for those parts. · Other. | 1.2, 1.4 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

`product.md` describes specialized, task-tuned tools over plain text files the user owns, and names humans and agents working together as a goal. This diagram is that goal applied to the work itself: agents report where they are working in a plain text file, and a person sees it as one picture. The file is diffable and usable without ADP. It follows `structure.md`'s rule that a tool type is a module on the shared core: what this diagram needs from the canvas library is added once, for any later diagram, and is named for what it does (Requirement 10).

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 - The definition files come first

**User Story:** As a tool engineer, I want the agent activity diagram defined once, where every host reads it, so that future implementations can interpret it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work starts THEN its first deliverables SHALL be, in etalii.adp: `definitions/diagrams/agent-activity-diagram.dis`, holding everything about the diagram type DISL can express; `definitions/diagrams/agent-activity-diagram.md` beside it, holding everything it cannot, under the headings its siblings use; and the FBL binding for the activity file (Q2). No implementation task in this repository SHALL start before the definition it implements is merged there.
2. WHEN `agent-activity-diagram.dis` needs something DISL, DID or FBL cannot express THEN the language SHALL first gain it, in its specification and its schema, named for what it does and not for this diagram (Q7).
3. WHEN the definition is written THEN it SHALL use the names its folder's readme prescribes: origin `etalii/agent-activity-diagram`, language id `net.etalii.adp.etalii.agent-activity-diagram`, file extension `aad`.
4. WHEN a language cannot express something this diagram needs THEN the gap SHALL be reported to the user as a selection (extend the language, and how; or change the diagram; or other) before anything is added to a language. The gaps known today are D1 to D7 under *Whether the languages suffice*.
5. WHEN anything in this requirement is delivered THEN it SHALL be a pull request into etalii.adp's `develop`.
6. WHEN the definition files and this document disagree THEN the definition files SHALL win and this document SHALL be amended, since the other hosts read the definition and not this document.
7. WHEN the definition files are complete THEN nothing a second host needs to build the same tool SHALL exist only in this repository's code or in this document, the layout of Requirement 6 included.
8. WHEN this document is approved THEN the tool's page in the Notion "Tools" database SHALL say what the diagram is for and how it functions (its elements, what connects to what, the lists and their groups, links, placement, and that agents write the file), completely enough for another implementation to start from, and SHALL be kept true as this document and the definition files change (Q1).

### Requirement 2 - The activity file

**User Story:** As a developer, I want the overview kept in one plain text file, so that agents can write it, I can read and diff it, and no tool owns it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an agent activity diagram exists THEN it SHALL be one activity file with the extension `.aad` and its `.adp` registration beside it, whose origin is `etalii/agent-activity-diagram` (Q2).
2. WHEN a specification is stored THEN it SHALL have a name, a status that is one of **Pending**, **Progressing**, **Input Required**, **Finished** or **Archived**, and its tasks (R3).
3. WHEN a task is stored THEN it SHALL have a title and a status that is one of **Progressing**, **Pending**, **Input Required** or **Finished**.
4. WHEN a location is stored THEN it SHALL have a branch, which is required, and a folder, which is `Default` when none is given, and its pull requests.
5. WHEN a project, an agent or an environment is stored THEN it SHALL have a name, and an environment SHALL also have a kind (R7). WHEN a pull request is stored THEN it SHALL have a title (R4).
6. WHEN an element, a relation, a task or a pull request is created in ADP THEN it SHALL receive a ShortGuid as its id, stored in the file and never changed by renaming or reordering. An id written by hand SHALL be accepted as it is (R6).
7. WHEN an edit is made in ADP THEN only the bytes that edit concerns SHALL change: comments, key order, indentation, line endings and everything the edit did not touch SHALL stay byte for byte as they were.
8. WHEN the file is read THEN it SHALL declare the version of its schema, and a file of a newer version than the host knows SHALL open read-only with a finding rather than be rewritten.
9. WHEN the file holds keys the diagram does not know THEN they SHALL be kept on every write and reported as a finding of severity info.

### Requirement 3 - What connects to what

**User Story:** As a developer, I want the picture to always read the same way, from project out to environment, so that I can find where any piece of work is being done.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN elements are connected THEN exactly these relations SHALL be possible, and every other pair SHALL be refused: a project to a specification; a specification to an agent; an agent to a location; a location to an environment. A specification SHALL have at most one project (R1).
2. WHEN an agent already has a relation to a specification THEN a second SHALL NOT be made by a gesture in ADP (Q6). A specification SHALL be able to have any number of agents.
3. WHEN an agent is drawn THEN it SHALL be able to have any number of locations, and an agent with none, or with no specification, SHALL be reported at severity info (R2).
4. WHEN a location is drawn THEN it SHALL have at most one relation to an agent and at most one to an environment, and no other relation of any kind.
5. WHEN an environment is drawn THEN it SHALL be one element however many locations relate to it.
6. WHEN a gesture is refused under this requirement THEN the reason SHALL be shown where the gesture ended, naming which rule refused it.
7. WHEN a project has no specification, a specification no project, or a location no agent or no environment THEN the file SHALL still open and each SHALL be a finding of severity info (R2).
8. WHEN a file written outside ADP breaks criterion 1, 2 or 4, or names an element that is not there, or uses an id twice THEN the file SHALL still open, everything readable SHALL be drawn, the offending relation SHALL be drawn marked as a breach, and each SHALL be a finding of severity error that says where it is. Nothing SHALL be removed by ADP.
9. WHEN an element is removed THEN its relations SHALL be removed with it in one undoable step, and the user SHALL be told how many when there are any.

### Requirement 4 - Lists inside elements, and what is shown

**User Story:** As a developer, I want to see a specification's tasks and a location's pull requests inside the element, folded the way I left them, so that the picture stays small and the detail is one click away.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a specification is drawn THEN its tasks SHALL be listed inside the element and SHALL NOT be elements: a task has no position, no relation and no toolbox entry of its own.
2. WHEN a specification's tasks are listed THEN they SHALL be under four groups in this order: **Progressing**, **Pending**, **Input Required**, **Finished**; each heading SHALL show its name and how many tasks it holds, and a group with no task SHALL NOT be drawn.
3. WHEN a group's heading is clicked THEN the group SHALL collapse or expand, and the element SHALL grow or shrink to fit with its relations following.
4. WHEN a group's state has never been set for an element THEN **Progressing** and **Input Required** SHALL be expanded and **Pending** and **Finished** collapsed. WHEN it has been set THEN that state SHALL be stored, for that element and that group, and SHALL be what is shown when the file is next opened, on any machine (Q3).
5. WHEN a location is drawn THEN its pull requests SHALL be listed inside the element under one collapsible group, collapsed by default, with its state stored as in criterion 4 (R4).
6. WHEN the diagram is shown THEN a switch on the canvas SHALL show or hide specifications whose status is **Archived**, and they SHALL be hidden when it has never been set.
7. WHEN archived specifications are hidden THEN those elements and their relations SHALL NOT be drawn, nothing else SHALL be hidden, and nothing in the model SHALL change (R9).
8. WHEN the switch is changed THEN its value SHALL be stored and SHALL be what applies when the file is next opened (Q3).
9. WHEN a specification's or a task's status changes THEN the element's look or the task's group SHALL follow at once, and a task that moves to a collapsed group SHALL NOT expand it.
10. WHEN a specification is drawn THEN its status SHALL be shown on the element in words and by colour, never by colour alone.

### Requirement 5 - Links

**User Story:** As a developer, I want to jump from anything in the picture to the page or the folder it stands for.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an element or a list item is stored THEN it SHALL be able to carry a link, which is optional; a location SHALL be able to carry one for its branch and one for its folder (R5).
2. WHEN something carries a link THEN a link symbol SHALL be drawn on it, on the element or at the end of the list item's line, and nothing SHALL be drawn where there is none.
3. WHEN a link is a web address THEN activating its symbol SHALL open it in a new browser tab without giving that page access to ADP.
4. WHEN a link is a file location inside the open project THEN activating its symbol SHALL reveal it in the workspace tree, and SHALL open it when it is a file ADP has a tool for.
5. WHEN a link is a file location this host cannot open, such as a folder on another machine THEN activating its symbol SHALL show the location and offer to copy it, and SHALL say why it was not opened.
6. WHEN a link is neither an `http` or `https` address nor a file location THEN it SHALL be kept in the file, SHALL NOT be opened, and SHALL be a finding of severity warning.
7. WHEN a link symbol is hovered or focused THEN it SHALL show where it leads before it is activated.
8. WHEN a link is added, changed or removed in ADP THEN it SHALL be through the property grid, as one undoable step.

### Requirement 6 - Placement

**User Story:** As a developer, I want the picture to arrange itself as agents add to it, and to stay where I put the parts I care about.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the user drags an element THEN it SHALL stay where it was dropped, become locked, and its position SHALL be stored (Q3).
2. WHEN an element is locked THEN it SHALL show a lock symbol, and its context menu SHALL offer **Unlock position**; WHEN it is not THEN its menu SHALL offer **Lock position**, which locks it where the layout has it (R8).
3. WHEN **Unlock position** is chosen THEN the stored position SHALL be removed and the element SHALL move to where the layout places it, as one undoable step.
4. WHEN the canvas's own context menu is opened THEN it SHALL offer **Unlock all positions**, as one undoable step, and SHALL NOT offer it when nothing is locked.
5. WHEN elements are not locked THEN they SHALL be placed by a layout that pulls connected elements together, pushes all elements apart, and radiates outwards by element type: projects in the middle, then specifications, then agents, then locations, with environments outermost.
6. WHEN the layout runs THEN locked elements SHALL NOT move and SHALL act on the others as fixed points; and the positions it computes SHALL NOT be written to the file (R10).
7. WHEN the same file is opened twice, on any machine THEN the layout SHALL give the same picture.
8. WHEN one element or relation is added, removed or changed THEN the elements it does not touch SHALL move as little as the layout allows, and the change SHALL be animated rather than jump.
9. WHEN the layout has run THEN no two elements SHALL overlap, whatever their sizes, including after a group is expanded (Requirement 4.3).
10. WHEN an element has no relations THEN it SHALL still be placed on the ring of its type.
11. WHEN an element is added from the toolbox THEN it SHALL be placed where it was dropped and be locked there; WHEN it is added by an edit of the file THEN it SHALL NOT be locked.

### Requirement 7 - Notation

**User Story:** As a developer, I want to tell the five kinds of element apart at a glance.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a location is drawn THEN it SHALL be one element with a horizontal line splitting two fields, the branch above and the folder below, with its pull requests beneath them.
2. WHEN the five element types are drawn THEN each SHALL have its own shape and its own colour in both themes, so that a type is recognisable without its label and without colour.
3. WHEN a specification is drawn THEN it SHALL show its name, its status and its task groups.
4. WHEN a relation is drawn THEN it SHALL be a line without a label, since its ends say what it means.
5. WHEN the diagram is drawn THEN it SHALL use this host's theme colours, fonts and canvas controls in both themes, and text SHALL meet the contrast this host's other diagrams meet.
6. WHEN a name or a title is longer than its element THEN it SHALL be shortened with an ellipsis and shown in full on hover; an element SHALL NOT grow without limit.

### Requirement 8 - Agents write it, people watch it

**User Story:** As a developer, I want agents to keep the overview current by themselves, and to see their changes arrive without doing anything.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the activity file is changed outside ADP THEN an open diagram SHALL show the change without being reopened, keeping the view where the user had it, with the elements that were not changed staying where they were.
2. WHEN the diagram type is published THEN `agent-activity-diagram.md` SHALL describe the activity file completely enough to write a valid one by hand, with one complete example, and a JSON Schema for it SHALL be published (Q4).
3. WHEN the examples ship THEN they SHALL include an instruction text that an agent can be given, saying when to update the file and how to make each kind of change: start work on a specification, change a task's or a specification's status, add a location, add a pull request, finish (Q4).
4. WHEN a file changed outside ADP holds something the diagram cannot accept THEN Requirement 3.8 SHALL apply, and nothing unreadable SHALL be removed on the next write.
5. WHEN a file cannot be read at all THEN the diagram SHALL say so with the format's own error and its position, SHALL keep showing what it last read, and SHALL NOT write to the file.
6. WHEN an agent and the user change the file at nearly the same moment THEN neither change SHALL be lost silently: ADP SHALL write its edit against the file as it is on disk at that moment, or refuse it and say so.
7. WHEN an element, a relation or a list item is written by an agent without an id THEN it SHALL be shown, reported at severity info, and given an id on the first edit made in ADP.
8. WHEN an agent's change removes an element whose position was locked THEN the stored view state for it SHALL be removed on the next write and not reported.

### Requirement 9 - Editing by hand

**User Story:** As a developer, I want to correct the overview myself when an agent got it wrong or was not there.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the toolbox is shown THEN it SHALL have one entry for each of the five element types, and none for a task or a pull request.
2. WHEN the user connects two elements THEN the relation SHALL be inferred from the pair, since Requirement 3.1 leaves exactly one for each allowed pair.
3. WHEN a specification or a location is selected THEN the user SHALL be able to add, rename, reorder and remove its list items, to set a task's status, and to do each from the element's context menu or the property grid.
4. WHEN an element or a list item is selected THEN the property grid SHALL show its fields, each editable, with a status as a choice among its values.
5. WHEN an element is renamed THEN it SHALL be by F2 or a double-click, in place.
6. WHEN any edit is made THEN undo and redo SHALL work as for every other diagram in this host, and the file SHALL be saved as for every other diagram.
7. WHEN an activity file is added from the workspace tree THEN it SHALL be offered where every other tool type is, and SHALL be created as the two files of Requirement 2.1, empty.

### Requirement 10 - What this host gains, and what ships

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want what this diagram needs from the core added once, so that the next diagram that needs it is a module and nothing more.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module is added THEN it SHALL live in `src/diagrams/agent-activity-diagram` with the folders its siblings use, SHALL be found with no core file naming it, and deleting the folder SHALL remove the diagram type.
2. WHEN the definition is used THEN it SHALL be bundled into the module's `definition` folder from etalii.adp and never edited there, the module SHALL derive from it what this host's DISL runtime derives today, and a test SHALL fail when the module and the bundled definition differ.
3. WHEN the canvas library gains list items inside an element with collapsible groups, a link symbol, locked and unlocked elements, a canvas switch, and the layout of Requirement 6 THEN each SHALL be a library capability a module declares against, named for what it does, naming no diagram type; the module's client SHALL hold declarations and event handlers and no rendering of its own.
4. WHEN the activity file is read or written THEN it SHALL go through this host's FBL runtime with no parser or writer of its own in the module (Q2).
5. WHEN the module ships THEN it SHALL ship examples, written for ADP, that between them show: every specification status and every task status; an archived specification; a specification with several agents; an agent with several locations; a location with the folder `Default` and one with a worktree; pull requests; an environment of each kind, shared by several locations; a link of each kind on an element and on a list item; locked and unlocked elements; and a group in a state other than its default. One example SHALL be this project's own work as it stood on one day.
6. WHEN the examples are tested THEN a backend test SHALL open every one, assert it reads without findings of severity error, and assert that writing it unchanged leaves its bytes unchanged; and one fixture per finding of Requirements 3.8 and 5.6 SHALL prove that finding.
7. WHEN a fixture's bytes are what a test compares THEN `*.aad` SHALL be exempt from line-ending conversion by a line in `.gitattributes`.
8. WHEN the work completes THEN `docs/tools.md` SHALL carry the row for `etalii/agent-activity-diagram`, kind Diagram, moved with its state; the Notion "Tools" database SHALL carry the same row (Q1); and `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/solution-structure.md`, `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md` and `docs/diagram-module-client-api.md` SHALL be true of the result.

### Requirement 11 - Seen working, and covered

**User Story:** As the user, I want the diagram seen working where it is seen, and every criterion here claimed.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work completes THEN a `tests.md` entry SHALL cover, in a real browser and in both themes: adding an activity file and finding two files; adding one element of each type and connecting them from project to environment; each refusal of Requirement 3; collapsing and expanding each group and finding the state after reopening; the archived switch, and its value after reopening; a link of each kind activated; dragging an element, unlocking it and watching it move; an edit made outside ADP arriving in the open diagram, with a locked element staying put; undo and redo across each of these; and the saved file's diff showing only what was edited.
2. WHEN the layout is checked THEN it SHALL be on an example of at least two hundred elements as well as on the shipped ones, and Requirement 6.7 and 6.9 SHALL be asserted by a test, not by eye.
3. THEN jsdom SHALL NOT be taken as evidence of any of what criterion 1 lists, since it applies no CSS and lays out no text.
4. WHEN a guard is written for any criterion THEN it SHALL be seen to fail against a planted defect before it is trusted, and the task SHALL name that defect.
5. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets before the tasks card is raised and again after implementing.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module depends on core and never the reverse; every capability the canvas library and the languages gain is named for what it does (Requirements 1.2, 10.3).
- The backend is the only reader and writer of activity files; the client speaks gRPC, as for every tool, and changes pushed to an open diagram ride the connection's existing `Watch` stream.

### Performance

- A diagram of two hundred elements and a thousand list items SHALL open, lay itself out and settle without a perceptible pause, and SHALL stay responsive while it settles.
- A change to one element SHALL NOT cause the whole diagram to be laid out from nothing (Requirement 6.8).

### Reliability

- The diagram never discards what it cannot read (Requirements 2.9, 3.8, 5.6, 8.4), and never writes to a file it could not read at all (Requirement 8.5).
- Opening a file, scrolling, zooming, selecting and the automatic layout SHALL leave the file's bytes unchanged (Requirement 6.6).

### Security

- A link is content an agent wrote. Only `http`, `https` and file locations are ever opened (Requirement 5.6), a web address opens without access to ADP (Requirement 5.3), and no link is followed without the user activating it.

### Usability

- A gesture that cannot be accepted is refused where it was made, with its reason (Requirement 3.6).
- Every gesture has a keyboard path, including collapsing a group and activating a link, and every control exposes its role and state to assistive technology.

## Out of scope

Each is a later specification if it is wanted, and nothing here should be read as deciding it:

- ADP finding the activity out for itself: reading git for branches and worktrees, a forge for pull requests, or `.spec-workflow` for specifications and tasks. Here agents and the user write the file.
- A command or service through which agents update the diagram, unless Q4 is ruled that way.
- Several activity files combined into one picture, and one diagram shared live between machines other than by sharing the file.
- History: what an agent was doing yesterday. The file says what is so now.
- A status for a pull request, an agent or an environment.
- The other hosts (IntelliJ, VS Code, Eclipse, Notion). They build the same tool from the same definition files under their own specifications (Q1).
